text.brief: On April 8, 2003, the retired army surgeon Jiang Yanyong wrote that Beijing's military hospitals held far more SARS patients than the health minister had admitted.
text.record: Minister Zhang Wenkang had told reporters on April 3 that the city had twelve cases ([Yanzhong Huang, The SARS Epidemic and Its Aftermath in China: A Political Perspective (National Academies Press, via NCBI Bookshelf)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK92479/)). Time magazine published Jiang's account, and on April 20 the Party fired Zhang and the mayor of Beijing as the city's reported count jumped from 37 to 339 ([Yanzhong Huang, The SARS Epidemic and Its Aftermath in China (NAP via NCBI Bookshelf)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK92479/)). The virus had spread from Guangdong since November 2002 while officials suppressed reports ([The chronology of the 2002-2003 SARS mini pandemic (PubMed Central)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7106085/); [Yanzhong Huang, The SARS Epidemic and Its Aftermath in China (NAP via NCBI Bookshelf)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK92479/)). It reached about thirty countries and killed 774 people ([WHO: Summary of probable SARS cases with onset of illness from 1 November 2002 to 31 July 2003](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/summary-of-probable-sars-cases-with-onset-of-illness-from-1-november-2002-to-31-july-2003)). In 2004 the army detained Jiang for seven weeks after he urged the Party to reassess June 4 ([CECC: Chinese authorities free Dr. Jiang Yanyong from house arrest](https://www.cecc.gov/publications/commission-analysis/chinese-authorities-free-dr-jiang-yanyong-from-house-arrest); [Human Rights Watch: The Tiananmen Legacy, ongoing persecution of those seeking reassessment](https://www.hrw.org/sites/default/files/related_material/The%20Tiananmen%20Legacy_3.pdf)).
text.reading: The Party fired two officials and kept the system that had silenced the reports, which is Stratagem 21. It then detained the doctor whose warning it had acted on, so the lesson its officials kept was silence.
text.gapText: Data Architecture. The world's warning system depended on case counts from a government that controlled every count.
text.fix: Pair official case counts with independent signals such as hospital reports, travel data and sequenced samples, and act on the gap between them.
